first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that shortening onboarding and reducing signup friction improved activation and time-to-value. Verifying both records will distinguish which intervention is most applicable before running the single available experiment. Promotional pricing has documented retention risk and is not the best sustainable-revenue response.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding, prioritizing completion and time-to-value while monitoring activation, qualified revenue, and 30-day retention. The verified onboarding result improved completion, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing both current declines with strong sustainable-revenue evidence. Signup simplification is also promising for SMBs but carried a 1% retention decline, so it is not the preferred cycle intervention.

final2.rationale: Run a tightly targeted promotional-pricing test for price-sensitive SMB accounts facing immediate competitive churn, rather than broad discounting. Prior evidence supports acquisition and revenue lift in this segment but showed materially worse 30-day retention, so cap eligibility and discount depth, and require monitoring of qualified revenue, gross retention, and 30-day retention before expansion. This is an exception-driven defensive response, not a general pricing strategy.
